convert-jeffresc report
=======================

Every converted object adopts the provider or application JeffResc created
(managementPolicy: Adopt). Adoption writes only the fields in the spec: a field JeffResc
left unset (it applied its own default) is left unset here, so the live value stays.
The one exception is grantTypes, which is always written: copied from JeffResc's
spec.provider.grantTypes (v0.2.7+) when it lists any, else [authorization_code, refresh_token],
JeffResc's own default (it treats an empty list as the pair). Authentik 2026.5+ rejects a login
whose grant type is not listed, and JeffResc v0.2.6 and older never sent the field, so providers
they created on 2026.5+ have none and reject every login (JeffResc issue 279). Providers that
existed before the 2026.5 upgrade were back-filled with all 7 grant types (Authentik migration
0032): the pair narrows those to 2, as JeffResc v0.2.7+ does itself, and drops implicit, hybrid,
password, client_credentials and device_code. The dry run shows the change per provider.
Before turning dryRun off, read each object's Ready condition (reason AdoptionDryRun lists
`field: old -> new`) and edit the spec until the only listed changes are ones you intend.

AuthentikApplication web/spa
  files: authentikoauthprovider-spa.yaml, authentikapplication-spa.yaml
  notes:
    - provider.grantTypes defaulted to [authorization_code, refresh_token] (unset or empty in JeffResc, which treats both as this pair); if the live provider has more, the dry run shows them narrowed
    - public client: the template reads .ClientSecret, which has the same value in both operators (Authentik's, normally empty for a public client)
    - Secret spa-oauth keeps its name: this operator refuses to overwrite the Secret JeffResc owns (SecretConflict) until the old one is deleted with the old CR; see the runbook, or convert with --secret-suffix
    - JeffResc labels its Secret goauthentik.io/application=<name>; this operator does not set that label

AuthentikCredentialsTemplates (cluster-scoped; a platform admin applies them)
  jeffresc-80ffa7c8: namespaces web

Adoption gate: these objects use the operator's default connection, where Adopt is refused
(reason AdoptionNotAllowed) unless the operator admin allows their namespaces. Set the flag
--default-connection-adoption-namespace-selector, or the Helm value
adoption.defaultConnectionNamespaceSelector, to:
  kubernetes.io/metadata.name in (web)

Adopt mode: a missing match target is reported as AdoptionTargetNotFound and nothing is
created. Once every app is migrated and SSO login is verified, leave adopt mode: remove
managementPolicy, match and dryRun from every converted provider and application (final
runbook step in docs/migration-from-jeffresc.md).
